title: Multi agent feature stream run
first_prompt:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

commits.summary: application-core environment E1: a consumed primitive return under a deterministic query model
commits.body:
The effect check answers a modelled call whose result the handler uses from a declared CallModel instead of refusing it. The coupling policy is defined first, in lib/src/environment.rs: a deterministic read-only query answers with one function of its key, the same for both builds and every call. A declared nondeterministic or fallible choice is a different model, refused by name for now. The query is encoded as a table of 2 x bound keys and answers plus a default, passed as inputs of the generated observe method after the handler's. So the proof covers every snapshot, a counterexample is one environment, and calls are never coupled by their position. The witness names the environment it chose and is replayed on a JVM under the generated stubs. effects --environment FILE (and compare's) merges the declared calls into each entry point's claim. Anything the encoding doesn't take yet (throws, DTOs, String, field or receiver keys, non-integral results) is refused by name.

Also fixes an existing bug: the two builds' unresolved marks were offset by tag x 16, which is the NullPointerException bit, so the old build's unresolved reasons always named a NullPointerException it never had. The tag now sits above every mark bit. Only the text of unresolved results changes.

Verified inline: the new lib/tests/environment.rs (11 tests: a rewrite proved; a wrong key, an ignored rate and a wrong-branch event refuted and replayed; keys asked in another order and repeated reads proved; a call past the bound unresolved; the proof cached exactly and another bound a miss; the CLI flag), with tests/effects.rs (18), compare, foundations, application_core (14) and the 228 unit tests passing. Interface requests for main.rs's and compare.rs's stale --environment docs, and compare's uncounted decision, are recorded in the stream brief's Progress.

commits.summary: application-core environment E1: a declared nondeterministic operation under a per-call choice
commits.body:
The environment stream's E1 now has its second coupling. A call model with coupling choice and the per-call occurrence policy makes a call's result a function of its key and of the occurrence of that key in the trace, the same function in both builds: a second read of a key is an answer of its own, the n-th reads of a key correspond across the builds, and different keys are never coupled by position. A finite script stays refused by name (the brief's optional work).

Encoded in effects.rs as the query's symbolic table with each entry used once per trace: a call takes the first entry of its key the trace hasn't used, else the default. This is complete within the bound (any choice per key and occurrence is a table listing each key's answers in order) and sound (every table is such a function). The witness lists a key's answers in occurrence order and is replayed on the JVM under the generated stubs; the assumption, plan and domain name the policy.

Verified inline: tests/environment.rs (13 tests) proves the rewrite and two always-different keys reordered under a choice, and refutes with replayed witnesses a wrong key, one read where the old build read twice (which the query proves), two reads of one key in the other order, and two possibly-equal keys swapped (witness code = quantity); another coupling is another cache key. Every lib suite passes (unit tests 229, effects 18, application_core 14, foundations 5, integration 65, and the rest). The README's Modelled results paragraph, this stream's addition, describes it. Rest of the brief unchanged and current.

commits.summary: application-core environment E2: modelled failures, checked or not, under either coupling
commits.body:
A dependency's model of its results (CallModel) may now list exception classes beside its one normal result, checked ones such as java.io.IOException included; a void call may be modelled by its failures alone. Each entry of the environment table, and its default, gains an outcome input: k throws a new instance of the k-th class (made by its public constructor without arguments: its class, no message, cause or stack), any other value gives the normal result. So which outcome a call gets is part of the same function of its key (and occurrence, under a per-call choice) as its value, for both builds, and the witness names it ('(arg0=0) throws java.io.IOException'); the shrunk witness keeps the failing choice and is replayed on the JVM. A handler of a modelled failure that reads more of it than its class (getMessage, getCause, any call on it, or handing it on as a wrapper's cause) is refused by name (effects::inspections), never answered with an invented message; a rethrow, a class test and a null test are accepted. A failure class without such a constructor, an abstract one, or a NullPointerException is refused.

Reproducers in lib/tests/environment.rs (now 16), on a fallible fixture: a rewrite keeping a catch of an IOException proves; a newly missing catch, and the failure's event dropped or sent on the wrong topic, are refuted and replayed; a dropped retry of an unchecked RateUnavailable is refuted under a per-call choice (the retry is an occurrence of its own) and proves under a query (the dependency fails alike for a key); a retry loop that rethrows proves; reading the message or cause, or wrapping the failure, is refused; another failure or failure class is another proof-cache key. Every lib suite passes inline (unit 230, environment 16, effects 18, integration 65, heap 49, alignment 34, summaries 40, observations 12, conformance 10, application_core 14, foundations 5, compare 1).

Found, recorded under the brief's Progress as an interface request for the objects stream, which owns the replay plumbing: jvm_witness::run's main has max_stack = 16 and pushes every argument, so a witness whose generated method needs more argument words (beside two int inputs, a table of long results past bound 2, or past bound 1 with failures) fails JVM verification and stays unresolved, which is sound but not replayed. The unresolved reason now names the words needed, and the fallible fixture uses an int rate. The brief outside Progress is still accurate.

commits.summary: Loops record why they stop (the default workspace's kppsnzyn, copied here for the rerun)
commits.body: This stream runs its own workspace's copy of feature-loop.sh, so the fix made in the default workspace as change kppsnzyn is committed here unchanged, byte for byte, before run-streams.sh reruns this stream. A session that decides to stop while this brief's status still says working now gets a turn to set the status and commit it, and the cycle instruction asks for the status line to be kept current. The files are identical to kppsnzyn's, so the merge takes them without a conflict. Verified there (bash -n and a stubbed test of the new functions).

commits.summary: application-core environment: E3 waits on the merge of the objects stream's construction plan, status blocked
commits.body: This stream was rerun after the loop's stop fix was copied in as wvournln. Its Progress named E3 next: a nullable DTO response through the objects stream's common construction plan. The cycle checked whether that plan is visible here. It isn't: the plan exists only on the objects stream's branch (construction::root, check_plans, and receivers and parameters made by a plan), none of those commits is an ancestor of this stream's working copy, and here construction.rs is still Phase 0's hook, which refuses by name. The main brief allows integration only through the merge. Writing the DTO's classpath check here would be the object builder of the environment's own that E3 forbids. The shared type is already in place (Returned::Object with Identity::Fresh or Stable in spec/plans.rs), so the Progress entry records the plan for after the merge: the stubs make the response by the plan's constructor from table inputs, a fresh identity gives an object per call and a stable one an object per entry, and an inspection refuses unmodelled methods and fields, as E2's does for a caught failure. The 11:33 integration report shows conflicts only in generated or coordinator files (llm-dlc/README.md, index.json, traces/README.md, traces/metrics.json), none of them this stream's. No open finding is in this stream's files, and this run has no job pending. E1's and E2's own items are done, so the status is now blocked on the merge (and on the values stream's String adapter for the Q rows). Only the brief's Progress section changed, so there is nothing to test.
